newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Senator fraud allegations hit Australia govt - poll.
newsitem.headline: Senator fraud allegations hit Australia govt - poll.

text.p: Support for both the Australian government and the Opposition has dropped due to an ongoing scandal over fraud allegations against a key independent senator, according to a poll published on Tuesday.

The Australian newspaper's Newspoll found support for Prime Minister John Howard and Opposition Leader Kim Beazley had dropped to their lowest levels in more than 12 months as a result of the allegations against Senator Mal Colston.
"For the first time since the last federal election (in March last year), about as many voters are dissatisfied as satisfied with the performance of both leaders," it said.
The poll found 44 percent of the voters surveyed were satisfied with Howard's performance, while 43 percent were dissatisfied and 13 percent were uncommitted.
It found 39 percent of the voters surveyed were satisfied and dissatisfied with Beazley's performance, with 22 percent uncommitted.

Police are investigating travel allowance abuse claims against Colston, who defected from Labor in August last year and whose support is crucial to the passage of government legislation through the upper house of parliament, the Senate.

The government, the Labor Party Opposition and Australian Democrats, the third power bloc in the Senate, have demanded Colston step aside from his post as Senate deputy president, but he has refused to budge.
Colston, who denies any wrongdoing, was released from a Brisbane hospital last week after suffering an unspecified medical condition and is currently convalescing at an undisclosed location.

The poll found the Colston affair had caused primary support for the government to fall two points from The Australian's last poll two weeks ago to 45 points, its equal lowest level since the election on March 2, 1996.
Support for Labor remained steady at 37 percent where it has been since mid-March, but was three percentage points below the support recorded in February.
As preferred prime minister, Howard's lead over Beazley fell three points to 50 percent, while Beazley's rating remained unchanged at 24 percent and 26 percent were uncommitted.

The latest result compares with the Liberal-National government's primary vote of 47.3 percent and Labor's 38.8 percent in the March 1996 election that saw Howard sweep to power after 13 years of Labor rule.
The Newspoll surveyed 1,150 voters around the country by telephone last weekend.
